newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says peace in Chechnya was 1996 highlight.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says peace in Chechnya was 1996 highlight.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Monday that peace in the breakaway region of Chechnya was one of the most important events of the past year.
"I cannot state that the evil circle of intolerance and hatred has been broken everywhere and fully," Yeltsin said in an end-of-the-year interview with three Russian news agencies.
"The course for peace often suffers heavy blows. But I will pursue it unwaveringly. This is the course of the president."
Yeltsin sent troops into the North Caucasus region in December 1994 to quell its independence drive.
The troops suffered a series of humiliations at the hands of lightly armed but determined Chechen guerrillas in 21 months of bloody fighting.

Tens of thousands of people, mostly civilians, have been killed, many more made homeless. Yeltsin has said the decision to use military force in Chechnya may have been his biggest mistake in political life.
In the run-up to the presidential election Yeltsin opted for a peaceful solution which helped him win a second term in July.
In August, his then security chief Alexander Lebed signed a peace treaty with the rebels and in November Yeltsin ordered all remaining Russian troops to leave Chechnya.

Interfax news agency quoted Russia's military as saying on Monday that the pullout would be completed by January 5, well ahead of a presidential and parliamentary election in Chechnya, scheduled for January 27.
Yeltsin said in the interview that 1996 had been a difficult year for him.

The president, who returned to his Kremlin desk a week ago after a heart bypass operation on November 5, added: "Now I am ready to tackle the most complicated problems facing Russia... I should make up for the lost time."
